listener_enabled.description: When true, the plugin listens to `channel` and treats allow-listed messages as dev requests (autonomous mode). When false (default), the OpenClaw agent orchestrates the harness via tools and the plugin does not listen to Slack.

channel.description: Slack channel ID (e.g. C0DEVCHAN). Only required when listener_enabled is true.

authorised_users.description: Slack user IDs allowed to open sessions or drop control reactions

credential_service.description: Vault service name for the Slack bot token. Enables reactions poller.

allowed.description: Repos the harness can touch. Supports owner/repo or owner/* glob.

never_commit_paths.description: beta.114: pathspecs whose changes are reverted instead of committed -- generated trees that belong to the repo's tooling, not to any feature (e.g. ["okf/**"]). Configured, never inferred. Empty by default.

logging.description: beta.24: harness log verbosity. When level='debug', SDK errors (crystallise, lead, worker, adversary) log their full error object instead of a one-line summary. Vault-lookup and pat-routing failures also log the exact keys tried. Set to 'debug' during smoke testing to make credential + planner failures diagnosable without a code change.

level.description: Minimum log level the harness emits. Defaults to 'info' (current behaviour).

max_output_tokens.description: beta.99: output-token ceiling exported to the SDK subprocess as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Nothing previously set one, so structured calls inherited whatever the bundled SDK picked for the model id -- undefined for a model newer than the pinned SDK. 0 disables (inherit the SDK default).

price_overrides.description: beta.57 schema fix (drift): per-model price overrides for cost estimation, keyed by model id. Values are USD per million tokens.

auth.description: beta.4+ addition, beta.24 schema fix. Anthropic API key resolution: vault-first, then env fallback. Both fields optional; when omitted, harness relies solely on env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or SDK default behaviour.

credential_service.description: Vault service name for the Anthropic API key. Vault-first lookup key.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable to read on vault miss. Defaults to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

require_worker_context_strict.description: beta.99: hard-fail the plan when workerContext is still thin after the bounded re-ask. Default false -- ship the degraded plan with a warning instead of burning the session (the b98 failure mode).

lead_salvage_truncated_plan.description: beta.99: when both lead plan attempts are cut off at the output ceiling, salvage the well-formed prefix instead of failing with plan_failed. The salvaged plan is INCOMPLETE and is logged as such.

contract_test_path_reconcile.description: beta.100: rewrite a drifted TEST contract path onto the test file the sub-task actually committed, but only when exactly one unmatched test contract and exactly one unclaimed committed test file exist. Closes the b99 seq-3 failure. Default true.

contract_mismatch_escalation_enabled.description: beta.100: when a sub-task made a REAL commit whose files do not match the contract, pause in awaiting_clarification (resumable, worktree preserved) instead of hard-failing the run. The sub-task still fails verification; only the terminal disposition changes. Default true.

ledger_reachability_guard_enabled.description: beta.101: before adversary review, check every sub-task commit_sha is reachable from HEAD and fail the run when any is not, rather than reviewing or shipping a branch that has lost work. Default true.

plan_path_validation_enabled.description: beta.101: at plan time, flag filesLikelyTouched entries naming a file in a directory that does not exist and warn the worker to treat them as guesses. Advisory; never blocks. Default true.

plan_path_writeback_enabled.description: beta.103: after verification proves a contract path correction, write it back into the sub-task's filesLikelyTouched so later revise cycles scope findings against the real path instead of the lead's fictional one. Never widens a sub-task's scope. Default true.

lead_repo_scout_enabled.description: beta.104: run a read-only repo investigation turn before the lead plans, so the plan names real paths and quotes real code. Best-effort; a scout failure falls back to the pre-b104 blind plan. Default true.

lead_scout_timeout_seconds.description: beta.106: wall-clock ceiling on the lead's repo scout turn, ADDED to lead_timeout_seconds by the loop rather than carved out of it. Pair it with lead_scout_max_turns, which is the bound that actually holds.

lead_scout_max_turns.description: beta.106: hard ceiling on scout agent turns. Aborting the wall clock cannot interrupt a tool call already in flight, so the SDK turn cap is the bound that actually holds.

lead_scout_max_chars.description: beta.107: ceiling on the scout report folded into the planning prompt. Raised 20000 -> 32000 after b106 reported reportChars 20049, the exact length produced by truncating at 20000. Truncation is now middle-out, keeping the head (locations and conventions) and the tail (traps).

revise_max_adoptions_per_cycle.description: beta.108: ceiling on orphan-finding adoptions per revise cycle. Adoption widens a sub-task's file scope, and scope is what a revise cycle costs. The b106 revise on PR #932 fired 21 mapping misses across two cycles against the original smoke's two, because the adversary re-reads the whole branch each cycle and keeps surfacing adjacent issues; uncapped adoption would pull most of the branch back into every cycle. Candidates are taken in severity order, and info-severity findings are never adopted -- info is how the adversary records that a PRIOR finding was verified fixed.

revise_route_co_fix_owners.description: beta.119: also route a finding to the owners of the OTHER files its fix needs (the adversary's `relatedFiles`, plus any repo path the finding's prose names). The b118 smoke raised 'the upload route discards the kind/title fields the drawer sends' in all three cycles and fixed it in none: routing was correct, but the route file's owner could not act alone -- persisting the fields needed a Prisma column it did not own, and removing the dead dropdown needed the drawer it did not own. It reported no-change, indistinguishable from 'already correct', and the finding was re-raised until the cycle ceiling. Set false for pre-b119 single-owner routing.

max_cycle_extensions.description: beta.119: extra execute+review cycles the loop may grant itself past max_cycles when the adversary's finding count is trending DOWN and this run's own average cycle cost still fits inside the session ceiling and the per-user daily cap. b97 already detected this arc and merely asked the operator to re-run harness_revise by hand; the b118 smoke went 16 -> 8 -> 9 findings and stopped on the ceiling having spent $12.90 of $30, shipping four blocking findings its own report called small and mechanical. Both conditions must hold, so a stuck run (flat or rising findings) still stops on time. Set 0 to restore the pre-b119 hard ceiling.

workflow_scope_precheck.description: beta.119: when the plan intends to edit .github/workflows/**, verify the routed token carries the `workflow` scope BEFORE running any sub-task. The CI-optimisation run planned a one-line ci.yml change, executed it, reviewed it, and learned only at the push that GitHub refuses workflow writes without that scope -- answerable from the plan and a response header before the first worker started. Only a token that PROVABLY lacks the scope stops a run; fine-grained PATs and GitHub App tokens report no scope header and are waved through, since 'cannot tell' must not read as 'cannot do'.

scope_blowout_file_threshold.description: beta.110: out-of-scope committed file count at which a cycle is abandoned BEFORE adversary review, instead of folding the overage into the review as a `fit` finding. On ProjectThanos PR #932 an in-worktree npm cache was swept into a commit by git add -A; the check reported 12423 out-of-scope files, produced a finding, and let the run continue -- the adversary then hit its 900s timeout on a 12432-file diff and the session died having pushed nothing, stranding eight good commits. A diff that size cannot be reviewed, so discovering that slowly is pure loss. Set 0 to disable and keep the pre-b110 finding-only behaviour.

ship_when_no_blocking_findings.description: beta.109: end the review loop when the adversary says `revise` but no finding is diff-addressable at medium severity or above. The adversary writes `revise` while ANY finding is open, including the informational ones it emits to record that a prior finding was fixed, so a run converges to a floor it can never cross: ProjectThanos PR #932 went 18 -> 15 -> 17 across three cycles and finished with ten low, six info and one low convention finding, nothing at medium or above, over three separate revises. Medium and above still cycles, so this cannot ship real defects; the residual lows go on the PR body and harness_revise picks them up on request.

auto_resolve_satisfied_contract.description: beta.111: settle a contract mismatch from the branch's own history instead of pausing the run for a human, when every expected path the sub-task did not touch was already changed by an earlier commit on this branch. Findings are often written conditionally ("if the handler extends `to` unconditionally..."); a worker that reads the code, finds the condition already handled and commits only a test then trips the contract check. That escalated on two runs running -- b109 sub-task 2 and b110 sub-task 5, the latter idle for forty minutes at $2.99 waiting for someone to type "skip" -- on evidence the harness already held in git. Strict: one expected path never touched on this branch and it still asks.

early_exit_no_change_cycle.description: beta.108: end a revise cycle that moved the branch tip nowhere instead of buying an adversary pass over an unchanged diff. The b106 revise's cycle 3 dispatched five sub-tasks, four returned subtask_revise_no_change, and the run still paid for a full review. Applies from cycle 2 only, and only when a prior review exists to carry forward.

revise_adopt_orphan_findings.description: beta.107: when an adversary finding names a file no sub-task claims, let the nearest sub-task adopt it so a worker is actually asked to fix it. On b106 the help-content.ts convention finding was raised in both revise cycles, owned by nobody, and could not have been closed however many cycles the run was given.

resume_ledger_guard_enabled.description: beta.105: also run the ledger reachability guard at RESUME, right after a re-plan re-allocates the worktree. b101 ran it only before adversary review; the b103 smoke lost eight of ten recorded commits on a resume, then stalled before review, so the guard never fired.

basename_rescue_enabled.description: beta.105: on a single-file contract mismatch where the basenames match, the planned directory is absent from the repo and the committed directory is present, synthesize the remap and re-verify instead of pausing for a human. Only continues if re-verification actually passes.

file_written_accepts_rename.description: beta.105: accept a file_written contract when the path was added or renamed-to inside the sub-task's commit range, even though the blob's mtime predates it. git mv preserves mtime, so a correct move made file_committed pass and file_written fail on the same file in the same commit.

worker_timeout_max_attempts.description: beta.113: total worker attempts for a timeout-class failure, including the first.

worker_first_token_retry_multiplier.description: beta.113: widen the first-token watchdog on each retry (30s -> 90s -> 270s). 1 disables escalation.

worker_first_token_retry_cap_seconds.description: beta.113: ceiling for the escalated first-token window.

api_key_env.description: Env-var fallback for the Vercel token when the vault is unavailable or empty.

token.description: Exactly one of value | env | vault.

env.description: Env var name holding the token.

slack_user_id.description: Slack user id mapping an inbound request to this person. Auto-captured in vault/self-write tiers; manual in copy-paste tier.

github.description: beta.25 hierarchical GitHub routing: org -> person -> token.

gitlab.description: beta.25 hierarchical GitLab routing: org -> person -> token.

commit_identity.description: Legacy per-user commit identity (superseded by hierarchical name/email).

user_identities.description: Legacy: { slackUserId: { github?: login, gitlab?: login } }

onboard_service_pattern.description: beta.78: vault service-name pattern for harness_onboard token storage. Placeholders {userid} {provider}. Default git-pat:{userid}.
